properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL, AND NOT LEGAL ADVICE. Anthony, 2026-09-23: he and his brother, Alexander Theodore Sligar, should be the sole owners of reflow2; a PR from anyone else, once accepted, should become part of the project they own outright.

WHERE IT STANDS TODAY (measured 2026-09-23): LICENSE is Apache-2.0; NOTICE reads "Copyright 2026 Anthony Sligar" — Alexander is not named anywhere; every commit's author is Anthony; ~980 commits carry a Claude co-author trailer; the repo is public with 0 forks; no CONTRIBUTING, CLA or DCO exists.

IDEAS, NONE CHOSEN:
(a) NAME BOTH OWNERS — a short written co-ownership (or assignment) agreement between the brothers, and NOTICE updated to both names. Cheap. Without it, joint ownership rests on nothing written.
(b) HOLD IT IN AN ENTITY — an LLC (possibly the one behind flo2.io) owns reflow2's copyright, and the brothers own the entity. Commonly cleaner for licensing, selling, or enforcing; costs formation and upkeep, and entangles reflow2 with flo2.io's fate.
(c) A CLA WITH COPYRIGHT ASSIGNMENT for outside PRs — a contributor signs that their contribution's copyright passes to the owners (or entity) when accepted. This is the mechanism that actually does what he asked; a CI bot (e.g. CLA Assistant) can require it before merge. Counter: assignment CLAs deter contributors, and some employers forbid them.
(d) A CLA WITH A BROAD LICENSE GRANT instead of assignment — the contributor keeps copyright but grants the owners perpetual rights including to relicense. Less off-putting, and it still lets the brothers change the license later; it does not make them the OWNERS of that code.
(e) DCO sign-off only — certifies the contributor had the right to submit; transfers nothing. Does NOT meet his goal.

⚠️ AN HONEST COMPLICATION HE SHOULD HEAR: most of reflow2's code was written by an AI model with Anthony directing. US copyright protects human authorship; the Copyright Office's current position is that material generated by AI without sufficient human creative control is not copyrightable. How much of reflow2 is protected — and therefore how much any license or ownership claim can actually bind — is a question for a lawyer, not something to assume either way.
